extracted.intended_audience: scientifically literate general readers and practitioners (physicians, anthropometrists, geologists) reading Popular Science Monthly
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and observational standards for recognizing glacial action on landscapes and rocks (striations, grooves, erratics, drift), together with related anthropometric indicators (chest expansion, complexion) used to compare temperaments and vitality in large conscript datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chest-expansion as indicator of vitality
rubrics_metrics.description: A free chest-expansion implies a large consumption of oxygen, a corresponding degree of force and activity in the circulation of the blood, and proportional muscular vigor. In the table, a chest-expansion of over three inches is taken as the basis of comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use >3 inches chest-expansion as a comparator because expansions less than this may include men of impaired strength; interpret as a close (but not absolute) relation to general vigor rather than a sole measure of vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexion as broad indicator of temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Light color of hair and skin, and blue or gray eyes broadly define a group composed of the sanguine and lymphatic temperaments; sallow or dark complexion with black eyes and hair indicates the bilious and nervous temperaments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complexion groups are coarse and can mix temperaments; they identify broad tendencies (e.g., propensity to certain diseases) rather than single temperaments reliably. National characteristics may skew ratios within these groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lymphatic temperament — physical and mental traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical: heavily framed, large-jointed limbs, large wrists and ankles, large head, unanimated face, thick-lipped, pale, blue/gray eyes, abundant light hair, flesh soft and flabby, muscles small and slow; puberty late. Mental: passions move slowly, easily kept under control, moderate emotional development, retentive, logical, persistent, honorable, commonplace in daily life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with weakness in vital energy and shorter life-span; predisposed to scrofula, phthisis, articular rheumatism; often shows hereditary patterns. Temperament often blends with others, especially in women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nervous temperament — physical and mental traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical: below-average stature, small bones lightly covered with flesh, large head with dark-brown or black hair, dark/sallow/pale skin, hot dry cuticle, small compact muscles, unequal circulatory distribution (e.g., hot head, cold feet), rapid or irregular heartbeat; digestion delicate. Mental: great emotional tension, emotions may override reason, acute sense of right/wrong but personal application, high capacity for pleasure and misery, fixed opinions, little respect for others' opinions, proneness to intense sexual emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prone to nervous affections (headache, neuralgia, epilepsy, insomnia, hysteria), mental derangement more likely than in other types; sudden mental impressions upset glandular functions. Typical cases more frequent among males; many nervous elements may belong to bilious temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilious temperament — character and tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical phase: grave, taciturn, even morose; mind and body move slowly but surely; remarkable inflexibility of will, sound judgment, strong convictions, abiding affections, and great love for dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often arises by combining nervous excitability with lymphatic phlegm and added flesh; participates in differing disease reactions compared with other temperaments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of large-scale anthropometric tabulations with mean values
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ large conscription-derived datasets (e.g., over a million examinations compiled by Dr. J. H. Baxter) and construct tables using mean values without manipulation except necessary averaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such large tabulations can illuminate relations (e.g., temperament vs. chest-expansion, disease ratios) but require caution: difficulties include lack of a unit of measure and challenges in collecting consistent facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ratios (per 1,000) to compare disease incidence by complexion/ group
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare frequencies of classes of disease across complexion groups using ratios per 1,000 (e.g., respiratory, digestive, nervous, locomotor diseases) to reveal predispositions linked to complexion/temperament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret differences in context (e.g., light-complexioned men show predisposition to skin diseases and digestive/circulatory/locomotor conditions); avoid overclaiming causation from correlation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical caution: 'not proving too much' when interpreting figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical tables have the merit of 'not proving too much' and can show directions for study but may fail to demonstrate positive causation; figures are useful but commonly over-interpreted by anti-statisticians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistics to indicate directions and hypotheses for further research; avoid extending conclusions beyond what the data support; recognize confounding factors (e.g., inbreeding vs temperament similarity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Striae and grooves on rock surfaces as evidence of glaciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rocks in place, mountain flanks and summits, and exposed outcrops are gauged in long, straight channels (from a foot to eight feet deep; two to three feet wide), often polished and lustrous, with grooves diminishing to fine striae (sharp scratches) that cover surfaces in parallel series or diverging directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grooves often occur in groups like mouldings and have consistent regional bearings, indicating movement from highlands; their size and direction, polish, grouping, and continuation across ruptures are diagnostic of glacial planing action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directional consistency of grooves/striae to infer source regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grooves and striae often show the same regional direction and appear to 'stream' from the north or from associated highlands or mountain ranges; averaged bearings can outline radiations from hypothetical centers (e.g., Canadian highlands, Scandinavian mountains, Alps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use average orientations over regions to infer flow directions of past ice; local deviations occur but main trends point toward distant source highlands that dominated the erosive agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of grooves/striations (grouping, depth variation, floor irregularities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grooves occur in groups and series identical in direction, may be crowded like rulings, vary in depth and sinuosity, and their floors may rise and fall as though 'hitches' occurred when first planed; striae may be fine and cover surfaces densely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note both macro- (deep grooves) and micro- (fine striae) features; variability (sinuosity, depth changes) provides clues to the nature and dynamics of the erosive agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drift / erratics — transported boulders as evidence of ice transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of enormous rocks (erratics) of lithology distinct from local geology—sometimes weighing thousands of tons—planted in fields, caps of cliffs, or strewn across areas where no like rock is in place; their composition matches distant mountain sources (e.g., Scandinavian, Alpine), indicating long-distance carriage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace lithological identity to probable source regions; note occurrence at elevations (2,000–3,500 ft and higher) and alignments that suggest transport paths. Use erratics in combination with striae and drift deposits to argue for glacial transport rather than local origin or mythic explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributional patterns of erratics and drift to reconstruct transport paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Erratics and associated smaller stones occur in alignments and fields, extend for miles in consistent directions, and can be used to trace probable transmission routes from source mountains across valleys and plains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey many instances to identify general transport trends (e.g., southeasterly alignments from Vermont granites across Massachusetts); corroborate with striae directions and lithologic matches for a robust reconstruction of ice movement.
